team|National team]]}} }} }} '''Hidayet''' "'''Hedo'''" '''Türkoğlu''' ({{IPA|tr|hidaːˈjet ˈtyɾkoːɫu}}; born March 19, 1979) is a Turkish [[basketball]] executive and former professional player. A {{convert|6|ft|10|in|abbr=on}} forward,{{Cite web|title=Hedo Turkoglu|url=https://stats.nba.com/player/2045/|website=NBA stats (nba.com)}} Türkoğlu played for six teams in his 15-season career in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He won the [[NBA Most Improved Player Award|NBA's Most Improved Player]] for the [[2007–08 NBA season]] and played in the NBA Finals for the Magic in [[2009 NBA Finals|2009]]. He also played for Turkey's national team in international competition. Türkoğlu has served as president of the [[Turkish Basketball Federation]] since October 2016. ==Professional career== ===Efes Pilsen (1996–2000)=== Türkoğlu joined [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Efes Pilsen]] (now known as [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]]) in 1996 and played four seasons with the team. He averaged 8.4 points on 58 percent shooting in 50 games in the [[EuroLeague]]. Türkoğlu helped the team reach the [[2000 EuroLeague Final Four]], averaging 13.6 points, 4.6 rebounds, and 2.7 assists, in 22 games.{{Cite web|url=http://www.fibaeurope.com/compID_,Uz02qBnJiADOq5VntEf53.season_2000.roundID_65.teamID_1338.playerID_21687.html|title=Hidayet Türkoglu | EuroLeague Men (2000) | FIBA Europe|website=fibaeurope.com}}{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/hidayet_turkoglu/bio |title=Hedo Turkoglu Stats, Video, Bio, Profile |work=NBA.com |access-date=November 19, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131212001316/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/hidayet_turkoglu/bio |archive-date=December 12, 2013 }} ===Sacramento Kings (2000–2003)=== Türkoğlu was selected by the [[Sacramento Kings]] with the 16th pick of the [[2000 NBA draft]]. He was the first Turkish-born player in NBA history.{{cite web|author=Contact rickchand: Comment|url=http://deadspin.com/sports/nba/five-tiny-tidbits-on-the-orlando-magic-207768.php|title=Five Tiny Tidbits On: The Orlando Magic|publisher=Deadspin.com|date=October 16, 2006|access-date=December 26, 2011|archive-date=September 20, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100920164611/http://deadspin.com/sports/nba/five-tiny-tidbits-on-the-orlando-magic-207768.php|url-status=dead}} He played alongside other European stars such as [[Vlade Divac]] and [[Peja Stojaković]]. Turkoglu received votes for the [[NBA Sixth Man of the Year Award]] following the 2001–02 season,{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/awards/awards_2002.html|title=2001-02 NBA Awards Voting|website=Basketball-Reference.com}} when he averaged 10.1 points and 4.5 rebounds per game.{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/t/turkohe01.html|title=Hedo Türkoğlu Stats|website=Basketball-Reference.com}} ===San Antonio Spurs (2003–2004)=== During the 2003 offseason, Türkoğlu was traded to the [[San Antonio Spurs]] along with [[Ron Mercer]] in a three-team trade. The trade also sent [[Brad Miller (basketball player)|Brad Miller]] to the Kings and [[Scot Pollard]] and [[Danny Ferry]] to the Pacers. Türkoğlu played one season with the Spurs and averaged 9.2 points on a career-high 42 percent three-point shooting.{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/t/turkohe01.html|title=Hedo Türkoğlu Career Stats|publisher=Basketball Reference|access-date=1 December 2022}} ===Orlando Magic (2004–2009)=== [[File:Hedo Turkoglu point guard 11-27-08.jpg|thumb|upright|Türkoğlu with the [[Orlando Magic]] in 2008]] [[File:Hedo Turkoglu 11-27-08.jpg|thumb|upright|left|Türkoğlu in an NBA game against the Washington Wizards in November 2008]] Türkoğlu joined the [[Orlando Magic]] in 2004, signing a six-year, $38 million contract. He scored a career-high 39 points twice: in an April 2007 game against the [[Toronto Raptors]], and in a March 2008 game against the [[Washington Wizards]].{{cite web|last=Scanlon|first=Dick|url=http://www.theledger.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=/20070405/NEWS/704050521/1011/SPORTS04|title=Turkoglu's Hot Hand Can't Save Magic as Raptors Pull Off Win|publisher=Theledger.com|date=April 5, 2007|access-date=December 26, 2011|archive-date=January 8, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190108151050/https://www.theledger.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=%2F20070405%2FNEWS%2F704050521%2F1011%2FSPORTS04|url-status=dead}} On April 28, 2008, Türkoğlu was named the [[NBA Most Improved Player Award|NBA's Most Improved Player]] for the [[2007–08 NBA season]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.seattlepi.com/scorecard/nbanews.asp?articleID=232732|title=Orlando's Turkoglu named most improved}}{{cite web|url=http://afp.google.com/article/ALeqM5hm0xnayvZmPtZhLNrFeZUNKFk3fQ |title=Turkey's Turkoglu named NBA's Most Improved Player |date=April 28, 2008 |access-date=December 26, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111218115747/http://afp.google.com/article/ALeqM5hm0xnayvZmPtZhLNrFeZUNKFk3fQ |archive-date=December 18, 2011 }} The Magic won 52 games that season, and Türkoğlu averaged career-highs in points per game (19.5), rebounds per game (5.7), and assists per game (5.0) and started all 82 regular-season games.{{citation needed|date=December 2019}} In the [[2008–09 NBA season]], Türkoğlu helped the Magic reach the [[2009 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]]{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/hedo-turkoglu-retires-after-15-seasons-will-be-honored-by-magic/|title=Hedo Turkoglu retires after 15 seasons, will be honored by Magic|website=CBSSports.com|date=November 13, 2015 }} for the first time since 1995.{{Cite news |date=2009-06-04 |title=Bryant torches Magic in NBA final opener |url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/basketball/bryant-torches-magic-in-nba-final-opener-1.821663 |access-date=2025-01-10 |work=[[CBC News]] |agency=[[Associated Press]]}} He led the Magic with 18.0 points per game in the Finals.{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/playoffs/2009-nba-finals-magic-vs-lakers.html|title=2009 NBA Finals - Orlando Magic vs. Los Angeles Lakers|website=Basketball-Reference.com}} However, they lost in five games to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]]. Türkoğlu decided to opt out of his contract after the season.{{Cite web |title=It’s official: Turkoglu joins Raptors |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/basketball/nba/turkoglu-raptors-2/?sn |access-date=2026-01-10 |language=en}} ===Toronto Raptors (2009–2010)=== [[File:Hedo turkoglu magic v raptors (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|Türkoğlu with the Raptors in 2009]] On July 9, 2009, Türkoğlu signed a five-year, $53 million contract and was traded to the [[Toronto Raptors]] as a via a four-team sign-and trade deal among the Raptors, [[Orlando Magic]], [[Dallas Mavericks]] and [[Memphis Grizzlies]], which also included [[Shawn Marion]]. As part of the deal, the Magic received cash considerations from Dallas and Toronto as compensation.{{cite web|title=Raptors Acquire Turkoglu, George and Wright|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/turkoglu_acquired_070909.html|work=[[NBA.com]]|date=July 9, 2009|access-date=July 9, 2009}} On March 28, 2010, Türkoğlu was a healthy scratch for the Raptors, his first benching since March 10, 2006, when he was still an Orlando Magic player. This was a disciplinary measure, after he was spotted by fans out late in a nightclub in the [[Yorkville, Toronto|Yorkville district of Toronto]], immediately after missing a game due to a stomach virus. The fans wrote staff within the Raptors organization, who then notified management and coaching staff, leading to the punishment.{{cite web|url=https://torontolife.com/city/raptors-hedo-turkoglu-caught-partying-in-yorkville-when-he-should-have-been-vomiting-at-home/|title=Raptors' Hedo Turkoglu caught partying in Yorkville when he should have been vomiting at home|work=[[Toronto Life]]|date=March 29, 2010|access-date=April 13, 2021}}{{cite news| url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/sports/turkoglu-benched-after-reports-of-his-late-nights/article1515426/| location=Toronto| work=The Globe and Mail | title=Turkoglu benched after reports of his late nights| date=August 23, 2012}} On May 29, 2010, Türkoğlu said in a television interview in Turkey that he felt he was wronged by the Raptors' management and wanted to leave Toronto.{{cite web|url=http://www.ntvmsnbc.com/id/25100585/|title='Toronto'ya dönmek istemiyorum'|work=ntvmsnbc.com|date=May 28, 2010|access-date=November 19, 2013}} ===Phoenix Suns (2010)=== On July 14, 2010, he was traded to the [[Phoenix Suns]] for [[Leandro Barbosa]] and [[Dwayne Jones (basketball)|Dwayne Jones]].{{cite web|title=Suns Acquire Hedo Turkoglu| url=https://www.nba.com/suns/news/turkoglu_signing_100714.html|work=[[NBA.com]]|date=July 14, 2009|access-date=July 14, 2010}} ===Return to Orlando (2010–2014)=== On December 18, 2010, Türkoğlu was traded back to the [[Orlando Magic]] along with [[Jason Richardson]] and [[Earl Clark]] for [[Vince Carter]], [[Marcin Gortat]], [[Mickaël Piétrus]], [[Nikola Mirotić|a 2011 first-round draft pick]], and $3 million cash.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/news_sunsdeal_121810.html|title=Magic Receive Turkoglu, Richardson & Clark From Suns|work=[[NBA.com]]|date=December 18, 2010|access-date=December 18, 2010}} On February 13, 2013, Türkoğlu was suspended for 20 games after testing positive for [[methenolone]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2013/news/02/13/turkoglu-suspended-official-release/index.html|title=Magic's Hedo Turkoglu suspended 20 games|work=[[NBA.com]]|date=February 13, 2013|access-date=February 13, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150214043351/http://www.nba.com/2013/news/02/13/turkoglu-suspended-official-release/index.html|archive-date=February 14, 2015|url-status=dead}} Türkoğlu said that he received medicine containing methenolone from a trainer in Turkey, though he did not know it was a banned substance.{{Cite web|url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/orlando-magic/os-hedo-turkoglu-suspended-20130213-post.html|title=Hedo Turkoglu suspended 20 games by NBA for violating league's drug policy|first=By Josh Robbins, Orlando|last=Sentinel|website=orlandosentinel.com|date=February 14, 2013 }} On January 3, 2014, Türkoğlu was waived by the Magic. He did not appear for them in the 2013–14 season.{{cite web | url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-waive-hedo-turkoglu | title=Magic Waive Hedo Turkoglu | work=NBA.com | publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. | date=January 3, 2014 | access-date=January 5, 2013}} ===Los Angeles Clippers (2014–2015)=== On January 16, 2014, Türkoğlu signed with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] for the rest of the 2013–14 season.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/clippers-sign-forward-hedo-turkoglu|title=CLIPPERS SIGN FORWARD HEDO TURKOGLU|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=January 16, 2014|access-date=January 16, 2014}} On January 18, he made his Clippers debut. In 13 minutes he recorded 4 points, 2 rebounds and 1 assist in a 92–106 loss to the Indiana Pacers.{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140118/LACIND/gameinfo.html|title=Notebook: Pacers 106, Clippers 92|website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=January 19, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160330123852/http://www.nba.com/games/20140118/LACIND/gameinfo.html|archive-date=March 30, 2016|url-status=dead}} On September 12, 2014, he re-signed with the Clippers.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/clippers-re-sign-hedo-turkoglu|title=CLIPPERS RE-SIGN HEDO TURKOGLU|website=Los Angeles Clippers}} ==International career== [[file:Basketball World Cup 2010 Turkey2.jpg|thumb|upright|Türkoğlu with the Turkish national team during the [[2010 FIBA World Championship|2010 World Championship]]]] Türkoğlu was a member of the [[Turkish national basketball team|Turkish national team]] which won a silver medal at [[EuroBasket 2001]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/hidayet-turkoglu-appointed-turkish-basketballs-ceo-91215|title=Hidayet Türkoğlu appointed Turkish basketball's CEO - Turkish News|website=Hürriyet Daily News|date=November 16, 2015 }} He averaged 15.5 points per game in the tournament.{{Cite web|url=https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/team/p/sid/2235/tid/376/_/2001_European_Championship_for_Men/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100122205744/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/team/p/sid/2235/tid/376/_/2001_European_Championship_for_Men/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 22, 2010|title=Turkey | 2001 European Championship for Men|website=archive.fiba.com}}{{Cite web|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2014/news/TUR-Turkoglu-calls-it-day-with-Turkey|title=TUR - Turkoglu calls it a day with Turkey|website=FIBA.basketball}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.aa.com.tr/en/sports/hedo-retires-from-international-basketball/172406|title=Hedo retires from international basketball|website=aa.com.tr}} Türkoğlu was named to the preliminary roster for the [[2006 World Basketball Championship|2006 World Championship]]. However, he declined the invitation.{{Cite web|url=http://findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_qn4188/is_20060613/ai_n16478551|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080105052001/http://findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_qn4188/is_20060613/ai_n16478551|url-status=usurped|archive-date=January 5, 2008|work=Deseret News (Salt Lake City) Newspaper|title=Injury? Okur declines Turkish invite|date=January 5, 2008}} In 2009, Türkoğlu was a member of the Turkish national team which finished in eighth place at the [[2009 EuroBasket|EuroBasket in Poland]].{{cite web|url=http://www.eurobasket2009.org/en/cid_toT,ovGDH2EaLKL67XnPo2.pageID_zfjpbftuHHkRSpqxSx8sT2.compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2009.roundID_6328.teamID_376.html |title=EuroBasket 2009 Poland |access-date=April 24, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110814035804/http://www.eurobasket2009.org/en/cid_toT%2CovGDH2EaLKL67XnPo2.pageID_zfjpbftuHHkRSpqxSx8sT2.compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2009.roundID_6328.teamID_376.html |archive-date=August 14, 2011 }} One year later, Turkoglu participated in the [[2010 FIBA World Championship]], in his home country of Turkey. The Turkish national team finished with the silver medal, having beaten every team except for [[United States men's national basketball team|Team USA]], the champions. Türkoğlu averaged 12.3 points, 4.2 rebounds, and 3.4 assists per game. At the [[2011 EuroBasket]], and the [[2013 EuroBasket]], he averaged 10.6 and 7.3 points per game, respectively.{{Cite web |url=http://turkey2010.fiba.com/pages/eng/fe/10/fwcm/player/p/pid/21687/sid/4728/tid/376/profile.html |title=Hedo Türkoğlu – 2010 FIBA World Championship |access-date=August 28, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160112032325/http://turkey2010.fiba.com/pages/eng/fe/10/fwcm/player/p/pid/21687/sid/4728/tid/376/profile.html |archive-date=January 12, 2016 |url-status=dead }} In March 2014, Türkoğlu retired from international basketball.{{Cite web |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/national-teams/national-teams/115089/hedo-turkoglu-announces-his-retirement-from-turkish-nt.html |title=Hedo Turkoglu announces his retirement from Turkish NT 4, 2016 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }}Türkoğlu was inducted into the [[FIBA Hall of Fame]] in 2026.{{cite news|title=2026 Class of FIBA Hall of Fame: Hedo Türkoğlu|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/news/2026-fiba-hall-of-fame-hedo-tuerkoglu|access-date=10 April 2026|work=FIBA.basketball|language=en}} ==NBA career statistics== {{NBA player statistics Clippers]] | 5 || 0 || 8.2 || .462 || .400 || .000 || 1.0 || .2 || .6 || .0 || 3.2 |- class="sortbottom" | style="text-align:center;" colspan="2" | Career | 98 || 72 || 29.9 || .406 || .350 || .751 || 4.2 || 2.9 || .8 || .3 || 10.7 {{s-end}} ==Post-playing career== On November 13, 2015, Türkoğlu announced his retirement after 15 seasons playing in the NBA.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/hedo-turkoglu-announces-retirement-nba|title=Hedo Turkoglu Announces Retirement From NBA|website=Orlando Magic}} He was subsequently appointed CEO of the [[Turkish Basketball Federation]].{{cite news |url=http://www.sabah.com.tr/spor/basketbol/2015/11/16/hidayet-turkoglu-tbfde-ceo-oldu |newspaper=[[Sabah (newspaper)|Sabah]] |title=Hidayet Türkoğlu TBF'de CEO oldu |date=November 16, 2015 |language=tr |access-date=November 16, 2015 }}{{cite news |url=https://www.haberturk.com/spor/basketbol/haber/1154000-hidayet-turkoglu-tbfde-ceo-oldu |newspaper=[[Habertürk]] |title=Hidayet Türkoğlu TBF'de CEO oldu |date=November 16, 2015 |language=tr |access-date=November 16, 2015 }} On March 15, 2016, the Turkish press reported that President [[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]] appointed Türkoğlu as one of his senior advisers.{{Cite web|url=https://www.dailysabah.com/politics/2016/03/15/president-erdogan-appoints-nba-star-hidayet-turkoglu-as-adviser|title=President Erdoğan appoints NBA star Hidayet Türkoğlu as adviser|website=DailySabah|date=March 15, 2016 }} ==Personal life== Türkoğlu was born on March 19, 1979, in the [[Gaziosmanpaşa]] district of [[Istanbul]], Turkey. His parents are [[Bosniaks in Turkey|Bosniaks]]{{cite web | url=http://www.takvim.com.tr/Spor/2010/01/01/bosnak_savasi| title=Boşnak savaşı| work=Takvim | date=January 1, 2010| access-date=October 23, 2012|language=tr}}{{cite web | url=http://www.sabah.com.tr/fotohaber/spor/12_dev_basari_oykusu/22450| title=12 dev başarı öyküsü| work=Sabah | date=September 16, 2010| access-date=October 23, 2012|language=tr}} born in the village of [[Lažani]], in central [[North Macedonia]],{{cite web |url=https://sandzakpress.net/jesu-li-bosnjaci-makedonije-zaboravljeni/ |author=Bajro Perva & Selman Selhanović |title=Jesu li Bošnjaci Makedonije zaboravljeni? |access-date=March 24, 2011 |date=March 24, 2011 |archive-date=May 11, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210511111028/https://sandzakpress.net/jesu-li-bosnjaci-makedonije-zaboravljeni/ |url-status=dead }} and he is fluent in [[Bosnian language|Bosnian]]. He is a [[Islam in Turkey|Muslim]].{{cite news |author=Tim Brown & [[Bill Plaschke]] |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2002-may-29-sp-lakerep29-story.html |title=Shaq and Hedo Share a Moment |work=Los Angeles Times |page=Page D.6 |date= May 29, 2002}} After moving to Turkey, his parents changed their surname from Ramićević ({{lang-sr-cyr|Рамићевић}}) to Türkoğlu, which translates as "Son of a Turk". He speaks both Turkish and Serbian fluently.{{Cite web |last=Klub |first=Sport |date=2020-07-10 |title=Brat Hido |url=https://sportklub.n1info.rs/skener/blog-ostalo/a336262-Brat-Hido/
